Let’s dive into Chapter 8: Navigating Interviews with Confidence and Authenticity.
Landing an interview is a big step—something to be proud of! But, let’s be honest, it can also feel a little nerve-wracking. The secret to making the most of this opportunity? It really comes down to preparation, knowing yourself, and being able to connect with your interviewer in a real, genuine way.
Start by doing your homework. Get to know the company and the role inside and out. What’s their mission? What values do they stand for? Have there been any recent changes or achievements? When you understand these things, you’ll be able to shape your answers so they show not just your skills, but your genuine interest, too.
Now, while it’s smart to practice common interview questions, don’t just memorize your answers word-for-word. Instead, focus on telling your story. Try using the STAR method—that’s Situation, Task, Action, and Result—to organize your responses. This helps interviewers see exactly how you think and work through challenges. For example, rather than just saying you’re a good problem-solver, share a quick story about a time you actually solved a tough problem at work. That’s way more memorable, right?
Here are a few more tips to keep in mind:
First, prepare thoughtful questions of your own. Remember, interviews aren’t just about them picking you—you’re also deciding if this is the place you want to grow. Ask about team culture, day-to-day dynamics, or what opportunities for growth look like. It shows you’re engaged, and it helps you figure out if you’re a good fit, too.
If you notice there’s a skill or experience you’re missing, don’t try to hide it. Be honest about the gap, but also share how you’re working to fill it, or talk about strengths you have that can help balance things out.
And let’s talk about nerves. They’re totally normal. Try some deep breaths, picture yourself succeeding, or use grounding techniques to stay calm and focused. You’ve got this.
Above all, remember that authenticity is your superpower. Don’t aim to be the “perfect” candidate on paper—share what you genuinely love, what motivates you, and what strengths you bring to the table. Most of the time, interviewers are looking for someone who’ll add something positive to their team, not just someone who ticks every box.
After your interview, take a moment to send a short thank-you note. Let them know you appreciate the opportunity and remind them why you're excited about the role. It’s a small gesture, but it really does make a lasting impression.
And finally, remember—every interview is a chance to learn. Think about what went well and where you could improve, then use those insights to get even better next time.
You’re not just interviewing for a job—you’re growing, learning, and moving closer to the role that’s right for you.
